trace.query: What should I do during a typhoon?

graph_hits.label: Approximate evidence
graph_hits.frame:
APPROXIMATE MATCH (not an exhaustive result): What to do in a typhoon
h:audience: All students
h:definition: Before: check the official LSPU-LB Facebook page for campus-wide class suspensions, and your professor's Messenger group and Google Classroom for class-level announcements, before you travel. Keep your phone charged. If you are already on campus in strong wind or heavy rain: stay indoors, keep away from windows and glass doors, stay out of open areas and away from trees, posts and loose signs, and follow the guards and faculty. Do not travel through flooded roads or walk under fallen wires. Go home only when it is safe, and check announcements before coming back to campus.

APPROXIMATE MATCH (not an exhaustive result): What to do in an earthquake
h:audience: All students
h:definition: During shaking: DROP to your hands and knees, take COVER under a sturdy desk or table (or protect your head and neck with your arms next to an inside wall), and HOLD ON until the shaking stops. Stay away from windows, glass, shelves and heavy objects. If outdoors, move away from buildings, posts and wires. Do not run out during the shaking. After it stops: leave the building calmly by the stairs (not the elevator) to an open area, expect aftershocks, and follow the guards and faculty. Help others only if it is safe, and report injuries to a guard or the campus clinic. Call 911 for serious injuries or fire.
h:sourceArticle: General earthquake-safety guidance (G), not an LSPU document
h:verificationNote: General safety guidance, not an LSPU-LB protocol. The campus's official evacuation areas and drill procedure were not supplied, so none are stated. Ask the Safety and Security Management Office.
